{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Gibraltar|Cuisine of Gibraltar]]

This meal is traditionally served with mashed potatoes. There is an alternative method made with a tomato sauce instead of brown gravy.

==Ingredients==

* 8 slices thinly sliced [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]]
* 4 slices of [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]], cut in halves
* 2 [[Cookbook:Hard Boiled Eggs|hard boiled eggs]], cut into quarters
* 8 [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]] (''con morrones''—stuffed with peppers), cut in halves
* 1 crushed or [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic clove]]
* 1 chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Stock|beef stock]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* Gravy powder (as required)

==Procedure==
# Lay out one slice of veal on worktop; place on it half a slice of ham, quarter egg and 2 olive halves.
# Carefully roll up the veal to make a package or roll with everything inside. Use two toothpicks to hold the roll together. 
# Place rolls on a plate and store in a cool place or fridge.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] garlic and onions until soft. 
# Add stock and two teaspoons of gravy powder and bring to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. 
# Carefully place veal rolls into the boiling mixture, being careful not to break them up.
# Lower heat and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until done. If sauce is too thin add gravy powder till the right consistency is achieved.
